subject: Myth & Symbolism
title: Minos the Judge
description: A micro-lesson that makes Minos the Judge usable.

hook.text: King Minos of Crete became a judge of the dead in Hades. His verdict assigned souls their eternal fate.

buildup.text: Three judges sat in the underworld: Minos, Rhadamanthys, and Aeacus. Each oversaw a different region.

discovery.text: Minos had the final word. He wound his tail—serpentine in Dante's version—to indicate which circle of hell.

twist.text: Minos was imperfect in life. He angered Poseidon. Yet the gods trusted him to judge the dead fairly.

climax.text: Greek judgment was personal, not automatic. A being with flaws decided your eternity. Justice was human.

punchline.text: Even the judge of the dead was once flawed.

quiz.question: What role did Minos play in the Greek underworld?
